title: feat(usage): rebuild the Usage page with the web page's sessions, charts and filters
body:

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

The existing Windows Usage page lacks the date ranges, contributor breakdowns and session detail needed to understand everyday usage and estimated cost.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

Users can inspect Gateway-reported usage natively, open a reported session in chat, export a complete report, or continue deeper analysis in the Gateway's web Usage page.

- Today, 7-day, 30-day and custom ranges; local/UTC reporting; estimated cost, tokens/cache, session counts, and a daily chart with an accessible table.
- Compact agent/model/provider breakdowns, bounded session browsing and inline details. Provider allowances, reset times and billing facts remain separate from session-derived estimates.
- Capability-gated search, filtering, sorting and paging. Missing, unpriced, partial, stale, failed and disconnected data remain visibly distinct from zero or complete results.

**Compatibility:** Gateways without a compatible `sessions.usage` API show an update/access notice instead of Usage totals. Older supported schemas use a bounded Basic view, not an exhaustive server search. No data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

Keep common daily analysis native without chasing full web parity. Heatmaps, per-turn/prompt-context analytics, transcript exploration and advanced exports remain in the web experience. The web handoff opens `/usage`; it does not transfer the current date range, filters or selected session.

The Gateway remains the data authority. Parsing, presentation and export ownership are separated from the native host, with cancellation and connection/query-origin guards preventing stale results or misleading exports. Original feature implementation: @bkudiess.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. Include before/after evidence for visual
changes when it clarifies the result.

validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

**All required CI passed for head `2953108c4a316ed275dc3b97912230ee828339b5`:** [Build and Test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/actions/runs/42795070620) and [CI Gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/actions/runs/42795070620/job/129768481415).

The run's `test-results-gateway-fixture` artifact contains **48/48 profile cases, 102/102 application cases and 1/1 released-profile compatibility case**, with no selected skips. The full fixture suite completed in 768.26 seconds; Usage's pinned-page case passed in 40.20 seconds.

Independent paired reviews covered the feature-repair scope; the final Tab-contract correction received a further scoped independent review. This is not a claim of a fresh whole-head dual-model verdict.

## Real Behavior Proof

<!--
Paste at least one current-head proof item that directly demonstrates the
changed behavior. Use copied live output, screenshots or video, UI diagnostics,
`winnode` output, raw MCP JSON-RPC, gateway invoke output, redacted runtime
logs, or linked artifacts.
-->

- Environment tested: local Windows ARM64 Debug non-Dev app and hosted Windows x64, both using isolated profiles and synthetic Gateway data.
- PR head or commit tested: published head `2953108c4a316ed275dc3b97912230ee828339b5`. GitHub tested merge ref `b647c7749e6546bfd19c4d6df978c391299ab6a2` with then-main `55ceb602`; the repaired test blob is identical in the head and tested merge.
- Exact steps or command run: the pinned-page command above, plus the hosted fixture/UI lanes in the linked CI run.
- Evidence after fix: the final local pinned-page fact completed 20 physical pane transitions, two opaque-occluder negative controls and 12 forward/reverse focus receipts across Light and Dark. Hosted `UsagePinned` also passed.
- Observed result: pane controls act on the owned window; obstructed targets inject no input; native Tab follows TitleBar, Dashboard, Notifications and Usage content, with the reverse/return identity checks intact. No shared-shell keyboard behavior was changed.
- Screenshot or artifact links verified? (`Yes`/`No`/`N/A`): Yes. The linked successful CI run and its `test-results-gateway-fixture` artifact are available. Obsolete screenshots and private session links are intentionally omitted.
- Not verified or blocked: Usage-specific live-Gateway/browser compatibility and billing accuracy, actual OS Save-picker interaction, whole-page High Contrast and localized visual fit. No final-head local Release UI run is claimed. The local Dark image was not settled focus-pixel proof; native focus receipts are the evidence for that transition.

## Security Impact

- New permissions or capabilities? (`Yes`/`No`): No.
- Secrets or tokens handling changed? (`Yes`/`No`): No.
- New or changed network calls? (`Yes`/`No`): Yes.
- Command or tool execution surface changed? (`Yes`/`No`): No.
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes`/`No`): Yes.
- If any answer is `Yes`, explain the risk and mitigation: authenticated read-only `sessions.usage` and `usage.status` use the existing operator connection and access checks. The page reads usage/session metadata, not transcript logs or per-turn content. CSV is explicit local output, not telemetry; cells are quoted and formula prefixes neutralized, incomplete exports are refused, and connection/query origin is rechecked across the picker.

## Compatibility and Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`/`No`): No for Gateways without compatible `sessions.usage`. Supported older schemas use the Basic contract; unsupported controls remain hidden and loaded-only drilldowns are not presented as exhaustive.
- Config or environment changes? (`Yes`/`No`): Yes. Optional `OPENCLAW_USAGE_RECHECK_INTERVAL_MS` and `OPENCLAW_USAGE_NOTIFICATION_MS`; normal defaults require no user configuration.
- Migration needed? (`Yes`/`No`): No data migration.
- If yes, list the exact upgrade steps: N/A. Update an unsupported Gateway when the page requests it. Dependency bootstrap and shared navigation are upstream-owned, not a Usage packaging migration.
